Subject: The frontispiece of October: the Academy's library at night in the Labyrinth. On a tall lectern an old book lies open, its pages lifting as if a wind came out of it, and from the page a tall cloaked figure is stepping out, seen only as an elegant dark silhouette against candlelight, more uncanny than frightening. Behind, the shelves of the East Stacks rise into shadow; a long stair climbs out of the stacks into the dark; a torn paper moon hangs high, ragged edge visible; three small bats cross it. Beautiful, hushed, a faerie tale about a story that got loose.

Subject: The Academy Kitchens at lunchtime, the most honest room in the Labyrinth: a vaulted ceiling blackened by three hundred years of steam, long tables scrubbed pale and carved with initials, a hearth big enough to stand in with a fire going, onions and bay hanging from the beams. Ambrose ladles soup at the hearth; Serenity and Wicker sit at the long table. One plain wooden chair stands pulled out a little ahead of all the others, as if it had arrived first and is waiting for someone.
